primary_finding.claim: Old/rotated-credential use IS captured by the audit log, continuously and currently.
primary_finding.detail: 85,062+ FAILED_LOGIN events for principal 'admin' on REST path /_cat/health, sourced from 172.18.0.8 (multi-node-wazuh.worker-1) and 172.18.0.9 (multi-node-wazuh.master-1) against all three indexer nodes. The FIRST such event on each source is 2026-08-31T07:27:35.169Z (worker) and 2026-08-31T07:27:35.469Z (master) - i.e. the exact instant of the Phase 83 admin-password rotation (credential backup id phase83-wazuh-indexer-admin-20260831T072701Z.bak, rollback plan phase83-wazuh-rollback-plan-20260831T073100Z.md). The most recent is 2026-09-01T00:32:59Z, still ongoing.
primary_finding.attribution_value_blind: The wazuh-modulesd indexer connector inside both wazuh-manager containers holds a stale 'admin' basic-auth credential in its INDEXER_USERNAME/INDEXER_PASSWORD container environment (INDEXER_USERNAME='admin', a NON-SECRET username). Phase 83 converged filebeat.yml on master and worker but the container-environment copy consumed by the indexer connector was not re-issued, so the pre-rotation (revoked) credential is still presented on every /_cat/health poll and is correctly rejected 401. Determined value-blind: no credential value was read, printed, compared, or hashed.
primary_finding.risk: LOW for confidentiality (the presented material is already revoked and grants nothing) - the audit log is doing exactly its job. MEDIUM for signal hygiene: this single stale consumer produces ~99% of all FAILED_LOGIN volume, permanently holds the failed-login-spike monitor in ACTIVE, and inflates audit-index growth.
primary_finding.disposition: REPORTED, NOT REMEDIATED. Fixing it requires re-issuing a service credential into two running production containers = credential + container-recreate gates. Out of scope for this read-only workstream; referred to the credential owner.

finding_weak_service_credential.severity: MEDIUM (pre-existing; unrelated to the audit posture itself)
finding_weak_service_credential.claim: The Wazuh dashboard service internal user (referred to throughout this artifact as DASHBOARD-SVC-LOWPRIV) carries a vendor-default credential that is BYTE-IDENTICAL to its own account name.
finding_weak_service_credential.how_determined: value-blind. The Phase 85 artifact leak-checker loaded every reachable credential value into process memory and compared it against the persisted artifacts; it reported a match for this account's credential. A follow-up in-process comparison confirmed only two boolean facts - that the credential equals the account name, and that the credential is all-lowercase-alphabetic. The value itself was never printed, echoed, hashed, fingerprinted, or written anywhere.
finding_weak_service_credential.consequence_for_this_artifact: the account's literal name cannot be written into any Phase 85 audit artifact, because writing the name would be writing the credential. Every reference is therefore the neutral designation DASHBOARD-SVC-LOWPRIV. Operators can identify the account unambiguously from its live attributes: reserved=true, backend_roles [], effective roles [manage_wazuh_index, own_index, kibana_server], and it is the sole entry in audit.ignore_users.
finding_weak_service_credential.pre_existing_exposure: the same account name already appears as an identity label in durable repository content that predates this workstream (root AGENTS.md and the Phase 84/85 evidence set). Those artifacts are durable/immutable and were NOT rewritten. This workstream neither created nor amplified that exposure; it is reported so the credential owner can act.
finding_weak_service_credential.disposition: REPORTED, NOT REMEDIATED. Changing this credential is a credential-rotation gate (dependency inventory, approval, backup, rollback, converge the dashboard container) and was not crossed by this read-only workstream. Referred to the Wazuh/indexer configuration owner and the credential owner.
finding_weak_service_credential.audit_relevance: the audit posture keys are unaffected: this account is denied the security index and the audit indices (tests N5-N14), and no credential value reaches the audit log (exclude_sensitive_headers=true, verified across all 140,642 documents).

redaction_note: Two fields captured verbatim from the live API - audit_config_live['audit.ignore_users'] and audit_config_live['compliance.read_ignore_users'/'write_ignore_users'] equivalents - list the dashboard service account by name. Because that name is byte-identical to that account's credential (finding P85-AUDIT-OBS-001), the value is emitted as <REDACTED>. This is the ONLY redaction in this artifact; every other value is verbatim live output.
limitations: A FRESH MISSING_PRIVILEGES event was not minted this phase. The only two identities with credentials available to a read-only workstream are the internal user 'admin' (all_access - never denied) and '<REDACTED>' (which IS denied, and was proven denied 10 times, but is present in audit.ignore_users so its denials are intentionally not audited). Minting one would require creating a transient least-privilege user, which is a security/credential mutation gate this workstream did not cross. The category is instead confirmed by live configuration (not present in disabled_rest_categories or disabled_transport_categories) plus live data (6 MISSING_PRIVILEGES documents, including the very Phase 84 .opendistro_security denial event) plus proof that the sink is writing right now (two fresh unique-marker events accepted this phase).
Scope is the Wazuh indexer cluster 'wazuh-cluster' (3 nodes), which is where security-auditlog-* lives. The separate shuffle-opensearch cluster is not part of this audit posture.
The stale-credential finding is reported, not remediated: remediation requires re-issuing a service credential into two running production containers.
No Class-A end-to-end evidence is claimed by this workstream.
read_only_attestation: Every request issued by this workstream was an HTTP GET, or a POST to a query-only endpoint (_search / _count / _ism/explain / alerting _execute?dryrun=true / _search/scroll). Zero PUT, PATCH or DELETE was issued to any Security API endpoint, index, index template, ISM policy, alerting monitor, role, role mapping, internal user, or cluster setting. The only DELETE issued was DELETE /_search/scroll, which releases the read-only scroll contexts opened by the sensitive-field scan and changes no persisted state. No user or role was created or removed. No container was started, stopped, restarted or reconfigured. No live configuration file was modified. The only files created are the additive, reversible artifacts under ops/reports/evidence/phase85/ and ops/reports/generated/phase85/.
secret_handling_attestation: No secret value, no secret-derived fingerprint and no password hash appears in this snapshot, in phase85-evidence-audit.json, or in any of the 90 Phase 85 audit reports. The admin TLS client certificate and its private key were referenced only as curl --cert/--key file paths; the key file was never opened or read. The two internal-user credentials used for the negative tests were read into process memory and handed to curl exclusively on STDIN via 'curl --config -', so they never entered argv, the process table, shell history, or any log; both were unset immediately after use. Credential-bearing environment variables read from creds.env were unset without being echoed. The audit index was never queried FOR a secret value (which would have placed the value into a query string and into the audit log itself); sensitive-field verification was performed value-blind, by field name and by pattern class only. The 68 compliance metadata bodies were fetched to a file outside the repository, analysed programmatically, and only structural counters were emitted.
